## CPAC 2023: "Call to Arms"

At the [[conservative-political-action-conference|CPAC]] gathering of March 4, 2023, Trump delivered an address that Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] called "one of his most raw speeches to date" and read as the opening of a new phase of the [[great-awakening|Great Awakening]].[{n}] In the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|speech]] Trump repudiated the pre-2016 Republican leadership — "We had a Republican Party that was ruled by Freaks, Neocons, Globalists, Open Border Zealots, and Fools... But we are never going back to the party of Paul Ryan, Karl Rove, and Jeb Bush" — and rejected "unlimited money to fight foreign wars, that are endless wars, that are stupid wars."[{n}] He told the audience that a second term would be more effective because of what he had learned in office: "I now know the good ones, the bad ones, the weak ones, the strong ones—I know em all!"[{n}] Trump also stressed his financial independence from donors, saying that his enemies "cannot stand that they do not own me" and could therefore never control the voters through him, and closed with the formulation "I am your warrior, I am your justice, and for those who have been wronged and betrayed, I am your retribution," together with the pledge "I will totally obliterate the [[deep-state|Deep State]]."[{n}]
entities/conservative-political-action-conference.md

At the March 2023 conference, [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] delivered the address later dubbed his "[[2023-trump-cpac-speech|call to arms]]," in which he denounced the old [[republican-party|Republican Party]] as one "ruled by Freaks, Neocons, Globalists, Open Border Zealots, and Fools" and named [[paul-ryan|Paul Ryan]], [[karl-rove|Karl Rove]] and [[jeb-bush|Jeb Bush]] as the leadership the party would "never go back to."[{n}] Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] wrote that the line's reception by the CPAC hall — cheers rather than the boos such a statement would have drawn in 2015 — demonstrated how far the audience had shifted, and treated the speech as evidence that the conference had become a venue for openly anti-establishment and anti-[[forever-wars|forever war]] rhetoric.[{n}]
entities/brad-getz.md

In "President Trump's Call to Arms" (March 7, 2023), Getz analysed the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], describing it as a "quotable masterpiece" marking "the beginning of the next stage in this war."[{n}] The essay is unusually autobiographical: Getz described himself as "a near two-decade long supporter of GWB and the Bush family in general" who found [[donald-trump|Trump]]'s 2016 demolition of [[jeb-bush|Jeb Bush]] "jarring to behold" but credited it with laying "the groundwork for my true Awakening."[{n}] He argued that [[neoconservatives|neoconservatism]] had blurred party lines and produced the [[rino|RINO]] faction, traced the pattern back through the Bush family to [[prescott-bush|Prescott Bush]] and their "fellow CFR infiltrators," and summarized it as "infiltration over invasion."[{n}] Getz linked Trump's rejection of endless wars to [[qanon|Q]] drops 119 and 489 on the auditing of war spending, framed the 2024 election as "a Battle for the True United States of America," and closed by pledging that Trump "intends to finish what he started, and I intend to help him."[{n}] The piece carried the standard disclaimer that Badlands features represent the opinions of contributing authors, and directed readers to more of his work at The Logical Faction Press.[{n}]
concepts/great-awakening.md

Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] treated the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]] as the start of "the next stage" of the Great Awakening, arguing that claims which were shocking in 2015-2017 had become "accepted fact" by 2023 and that [[red-pilling|red-pilling]] was spreading "from Twitter to TikTok, at family gatherings, online, offline, and beyond, as the Truth has grown impossible to escape."[{n}] He framed the period as "a great crossroads in the history of Mankind," writing that a century hence these years would be seen either as the beginning of "a New Globalist World Order run by unelected officials who view people as faceless workers" or as "the moment that Freed the planet and returned it to the People" — adding the maxim "How America Goes, so goes the World."[{n}]
concepts/neoconservatives.md

In Badlands commentary on the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] argued that neoconservatism was the mechanism by which the American right acquired its war-making reputation: for a century, he wrote, Democratic presidents had presided over the major wars — Wilson and World War I, Roosevelt and World War II, Truman and Korea, Johnson and Vietnam — and "it wasn't until Neo-conservatism blurred party lines, allowing [[rino|RINOs]] to emerge in the Republican party, that the right followed in the left's War-like footsteps."[{n}] He attributed the shift to the "Neo-con Bushes and their fellow [[council-on-foreign-relations|CFR]] infiltrators," traceable back to [[prescott-bush|Prescott Bush]], and characterized the process as "infiltration over invasion."[{n}] [[donald-trump|Trump]]'s CPAC line naming [[paul-ryan|Paul Ryan]], [[karl-rove|Karl Rove]] and [[jeb-bush|Jeb Bush]] as figures the party would never return to was read as the public repudiation of that faction.[{n}]
entities/republican-party.md

In the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] described the party he entered in 2015 as one "ruled by Freaks, Neocons, Globalists, Open Border Zealots, and Fools" and declared that "we are never going back to the party of Paul Ryan, Karl Rove, and Jeb Bush."[{n}] Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] argued that "the infiltrated version of the Republican party is dead" — its members "may still hold seats, but their days are numbered" — and cited the exposure of figures such as [[liz-cheney|Liz Cheney]] as proof that there was no going back.[{n}] Getz held that Trump's first term "drew them out and made us aware of just how different the Republican party was than voters realized," a claim he said was shocking in 2015-2017 but accepted by 2023.[{n}]
entities/jeb-bush.md

Jeb Bush was named by [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] in the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]] as one of the establishment figures — alongside [[paul-ryan|Paul Ryan]] and [[karl-rove|Karl Rove]] — whose party the Republicans would "never go back to."[{n}] Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]], a longtime Bush family supporter, wrote that watching Jeb Bush — "the candidate whom I expected to get the nod before Trump entered the arena" — be exposed during the 2016 primaries by "someone who wasn't afraid to be real with the American People" laid the groundwork for his own political awakening.[{n}]
entities/paul-ryan.md

[[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] named Paul Ryan in the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], telling the audience that the party would "never go back to the party of Paul Ryan, Karl Rove, and Jeb Bush" after describing the pre-2016 Republican leadership as "Freaks, Neocons, Globalists, Open Border Zealots, and Fools."[{n}] Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] cited the naming of Ryan as evidence that the "infiltrated version of the Republican party is dead."[{n}]
entities/liz-cheney.md

In Badlands commentary on the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] cited "the Liz Cheneys of the world" as figures who had been exposed as part of the establishment wing of the [[republican-party|Republican Party]], arguing that their political defeat demonstrated that "there is no going back" to the pre-2016 party.[{n}]
concepts/deep-state.md

Closing the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] pledged: "I will totally obliterate the Deep State."[{n}] Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] argued that Trump's public rejection of "unlimited money" for [[forever-wars|endless wars]] was itself a signal to the Deep State "that you know what it really is," since war functions as "possibly the biggest operation currently set in place to wash and re-distribute American taxpayer money."[{n}] Getz further contended that Trump's personal wealth had let him "traverse our Globalist Usurpers' Monetary Debt Control Matrix freely," quoting Trump's claim that his enemies "cannot steer me, they cannot shake me and they will never, ever control me and they will never ever, therefore control you."[{n}]
concepts/qanon.md

In "President Trump's Call to Arms," Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] cited Q drop 119, which asked "Who AUDITS the billions paid for war?", and post 489, which stated that "WAR = scam (trillions)" and asked "Who audits where the money actually goes? Who receives it?"[{n}] Getz argued that these January 2018 questions "made far less sense" at the time than they did in 2023, "over $100 Billion to Ukraine later."[{n}] He also referenced a 2017 Q post suggesting that 70% of elected politicians were corrupt, calling it "a tall statement at the time, but after all we've seen since 2015, easily believable," and crediting [[donald-trump|Trump]] with drawing "out the 70% like snakes."[{n}]
concepts/rino.md

Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] located the origin of the RINO phenomenon in [[neoconservatives|neoconservatism]], writing that it was only when neoconservatism "blurred party lines, allowing RINOs to emerge in the Republican party" that the American right adopted the war-making posture previously associated with Democratic administrations.[{n}] In the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] told the audience that "people are tired of RINOs and globalists; they want to see America First."[{n}]
concepts/america-first-movement.md

In the [[2023-trump-cpac-speech|2023 Trump CPAC speech]], [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] tied the America First banner directly to opposition to the party establishment and to [[forever-wars|endless wars]], telling the audience: "We have no choice. If we don't do this, our country will be lost forever. People are tired of [[rino|RINOs]] and globalists; they want to see America First."[{n}] Badlands contributor [[brad-getz|Brad Getz]] framed the resulting programme as the restoration of "the REAL United States of America" and a break from "the stifling system of debt slavery."[{n}]
